lines: If you're just starting with ChatGPT, this is going to help you a lot.
A year back I wasn't able to write a single line of code.
Now I build apps for my friends and for my own business.
Most people think building with AI is only for developers, and that's not true.
You're able to build a working app in a weekend if you pick one small problem.
When I was starting with ChatGPT I asked it really basic questions.
Things like, what is a database, and how do I put a website online.
It didn't judge me, and that's what helped me keep going.
My friends thought I was wasting my time.
Then I showed them the first app, and they wanted one for their business too.
So here's the different way I'd do it if I went back and started over.
First, pick one small problem you have every single week.
For me it was sending invoices for my business.
Second, describe that one small problem to the AI like you're talking to a friend.
Don't try to sound smart, just say what you'd want it to do.
Third, ask it to build the smallest version that could help.
Building with AI is different because you're not typing code, you're giving directions.
You'll get it wrong a few times, and that's fine.
I had to go back and explain the same thing three different ways.
But by Sunday night I had a working app that sent my invoices.
My friends were able to use it on their phones the same day.
That's the part nobody tells you about building with AI.
You don't need to know how to build everything, you need to know what would help.
So if you're starting with ChatGPT this week, pick one small problem and build that.
Follow me if you want to see the exact prompts I used for my first working app.
